header: Date: 2026-08-21 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 mins | Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Auriga Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Auriga Infra), Ravi Singh (Auriga PM)
summary: POC scoping focused on capacity sizing and autoscaling strategy for Auriga's LLM-powered search assistant. Discussed reserved GPU commitments vs burst capacity, fallback model variants, KV/prefix cache behavior, success criteria (latency SLO, cost per 1k QPS, correctness thresholds), and timelines for benchmark run. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send capacity proposal and benchmark plan; customer to share traffic histograms and security requirements.
topics: POC goals and success criteria; current infra and traffic patterns; reserved GPUs and burst strategy; autoscale triggers and warm pools; fallback policies and model variants; benchmark setup (datasets, latency/cost metrics); security and compliance notes; timeline and next steps.
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining - quick intros?
[00:08] Maya (Auriga): Hi, I'm Maya, head of ML at Auriga. We run the assist product, about 400k monthly active users, peak spikes during support windows.
[00:18] Liam (Auriga): Liam here, infra. We manage k8s clusters and some GPU infra on GCP.
[00:22] Ravi (Auriga): Ravi, product. I'll own success criteria side.
[00:26] Diego (Redwood): Diego, engineering for inference, I'll be driving the perf plan.
[00:31] Sophie: Great. Today we're scoping the POC - specifically capacity sizing and autoscale - reserved GPUs, burst, fallback. Goal is to make sure we model cost and latency tradeoffs.
[00:45] Maya: Our big ask is that during peak we keep tail latency under 300ms 95th for short replies, and under 800ms 95th for long generations. Cost target is roughly $X per 1k requests, we'll clarify.
[01:05] Sophie: Sounds good. Can you share current qps patterns?
[01:10] Liam: Yeah, we see baseline 120 qps, bursts up to 1600 qps during campaigns, spikes that last about 10-15 minutes. There's also nightly batch jobs hitting embeddings.
[01:25] Diego: Ok that's helpful - so autoscale needs to handle short high spikes. For POC we usually propose a reserved pool to cover baseline and predictable load, plus a burst pool that can kick in for spikes. The burst can be either pre-warmed reserved GPUs or ephemeral cloud GPUs depending on your constraints.
[01:45] Ravi: What's the tradeoff on pre-warmed vs ephemeral?
[01:48] Diego: Pre-warmed reserved GPUs reduce cold-start latency on KV cache - sorry, KV cache - and avoid model load time. Ephemeral GPUs are cheaper if spikes are rare but have higher startup latency. With long context or heavy quantized models the warmup can be 20-60s unless you keep them warm.
[02:10] Liam: We prefer not to have long warm-up windows; our user experience won't tolerate 30s delays.
[02:15] Sophie: Then we'll likely recommend a small warm pool for burst capacity, plus autoscale rules that prefer warm pool before spinning up new nodes.
[02:23] Maya: How do you handle fallback policies? Like if the preferred model is busy or out of capacity.
[02:28] Diego: We do routing policy tiers: primary model (high-quality), then a lower-tier variant (quantized or smaller architecture) for fallback, and finally queueing with fast 503-style signals or degrade to cached responses for repeat prompts. We can also route non-critical calls to a cheaper model.
[02:45] Ravi: Any impact on correctness? We need to measure regression against our eval set.
[02:50] Diego: Absolutely, we'll run the same eval prompts across both variants and track quality deltas. For POC we'll record A/B metrics - rouge/bleu-like or task-specific metrics you use.
[03:05] Liam: About KV cache - our workloads have a lot of prefix reuse, should caching reduce token cost?
[03:10] Diego: Yes, prefix/KV cache can reduce repetition; but shared caches across models or variants is tricky. We'll capture hit-rate during the benchmark. Sometimes transcription in logs shows 'KV cash' but we'll parse correctly.
[03:23] Maya: On security, we need SOC 2, SSO, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys. Any constraints there?
[03:30] Sophie: Redwood offers KMS integration in Private mode; for hosted POC we can enable encrypted at rest and customer-owned keys if needed. We'll share SOC 2 docs and network diagrams.
[03:40] Ravi: For POC success criteria: 95th latency targets, cost per 1k requests within X% of baseline, and no data exfiltration.
[03:50] Sophie: Let's capture that: latency SLOs, cost thresholds, and quality regressions under Y% - we'll formalize in the proposal.
[04:00] Maya: What about autoscale triggers - based on qps or GPU utilization?
[04:04] Diego: We typically use request queue length and p99 latency as primary triggers, with CPU/GPU util as secondary. For short spikes, queue-length-based scaling gives faster reactiveness.
[04:18] Liam: How fast is scale-up to burst pool?
[04:22] Diego: If pool is warm, traffic can shift within seconds to low-teens seconds. If spinning up new instances cold, startup can be 45-90s depending on model and container initialization; that's why we prefer a managed warm pool.
[04:35] Ravi: Okay can you propose numbers for reserved vs burst GPUs for our profile?
[04:39] Sophie: Based on 120 baseline and 1.6k spikes, a rough starting point: reserve capacity to cover 250-300 QPS (buffers for growth), and a burst pool sized for additional 1400 QPS in pre-warmed nodes. Exact GPU counts depend on model throughput; Diego will run bench estimates in the proposal.
[04:58] Diego: I'll include model throughput (tokens/s per GPU) assumptions, and also two config options - 1) conservative reserved + warm burst, 2) minimal reserved + more ephemeral burst. We'll show cost tradeoffs.
[05:12] Maya: For the benchmark we want representative traffic and prompts - Ravi will share top 100 prompts and cost targets.
[05:20] Ravi: Yes, we'll export anonymized logs and sample prompts. We'll also include a small eval set for quality checks.
[05:28] Sophie: Good. About metrics - we'll collect 95/99 latencies, token-level cost, throughput, and quality metrics. For the POC we'll run three steady-state runs and at least two spike-run scenarios.
[05:40] Diego: And we'll capture cache hit-rate, model load times, and warm pool effectiveness.
[05:46] Maya: Regarding networking - we need VPC peering or private link for compliance.
[05:51] Sophie: For Private deployment we can do VPC peering and your KMS. For hosted we can support private link or customer-managed ingress. We'll attach the network diagram.
[06:00] Liam: Are there any hard limits on burst ephemeral capacity?
[06:03] Diego: Not on our side, but cloud quotas matter. We'll coordinate with your cloud ops to request quotas if we need ephemeral GPUs. For POC, we often work within a conservative quota to keep setup quick.
[06:15] Ravi: What about autoscale cool-downs so we don't oscillate?
[06:18] Diego: We'll set hysteresis: require sustained signal for X seconds and use cooldown windows. For short spikes we prefer queue-length signal with short windows to avoid overshoot.
[06:32] Maya: Can we simulate bursts of varying shapes?
[06:35] Diego: Yes, benchmark scripts will include ramp, step, and long tail scenarios.
[06:40] Sophie: Timeline - we propose: share logs and prompts by Aug 24; Redwood to send proposal and benchmark plan by Aug 24; bench run week of Aug 31; 2-week POC (benchmark + validation) through Sep 14; presentation of results Sep 16. Does that work?
[06:58] Maya: That timeline looks fine.
[07:02] Liam: A couple of follow-ups - what models will you propose? Are you suggesting Redwood-verified open models or our licensed model?
[07:10] Diego: We'll propose two model families: a high-quality variant (larger, likely 20-30B float or quantized equivalent) and a smaller quantized variant for fallback, and we can also evaluate your licensed model if you provide the artifact or access.
[07:26] Ravi: On data retention during POC - we need logs purged after 30 days.
[07:30] Sophie: Noted, we'll include retention controls and deletion policy in the security docs.
[07:36] Maya: For success criteria on correctness - we'll set an internal threshold: for the fallback model, quality drop no more than 6% on your eval metric.
[07:44] Diego: We'll record that as a gating metric.
[07:48] Sophie: Anything else on the infra side?
[07:50] Liam: One ask - can the warm pool be fractionally sized so we don't waste GPUs? Like keep a few pre-warmed replicas with fast loading strategies.
[07:58] Diego: We can tune pre-warm to number of GPUs and instance shapes; warm pool policies allow liveness scaling (keep N warm, scale to M on demand). We'll show config examples in the proposal.
[08:12] Ravi: For cost modeling, can you show per-hour and per-1k-request math?
[08:15] Sophie: Yes, the proposal will include per-GPU hour cost, expected tokens per request, and projected per-1k-request cost under each capacity plan.
[08:26] Maya: What about observability - how will we measure token-level cost and attribute to routes?
[08:30] Diego: Redwood Console provides per-route token and latency breakdown, tracing hooks, and we can enable per-token cost attribution. We'll demo that in follow-up.
[08:40] Sophie: Ok let's go through a quick mock benchmark plan so you know what we'll do.
[08:44] Diego: Step 1: baseline throughput runs with reserved capacity for steady state; Step 2: spike simulations with warm pool; Step 3: fallback path validation by saturating primary model and verifying routing to fallback; Step 4: quality evals across variants. We'll collect metrics and produce a cost/latency tradeoff table.
[09:05] Maya: That looks good. Any blockers on your side?
[09:08] Diego: We need the sample prompts, traffic histograms, and confirmation of where to run POC (hosted vs private).
[09:15] Liam: We prefer hosted POC with private link, at least to begin.
[09:19] Sophie: Noted. We'll include hosted-with-privatelink option.
[09:24] Ravi: On success gating - if fallback model quality drops >6% do we abort?
[09:29] Sophie: We'll include gating thresholds; decision to abort or extend will be a joint call.
[09:34] Maya: Can you also include a list of required cloud quotas and sample IAM roles needed?
[09:39] Diego: Yes, quota list and minimal roles will be in the runbook.
[09:44] Sophie: Anything else?
[09:46] Liam: One more question on KV cache persistence across restarts - if a node restarts does cache repopulate quickly?
[09:53] Diego: Cache is per-host but we have strategies: prefix caching at ingress and shared Redis-backed hot keys for very hot prefixes. We'll measure effective hit-rate.
[10:04] Sophie: Ok I'll recap next steps at the end. Any final items?
[10:08] Maya: No, thanks.
[10:10] Sophie: Recap: Redwood will send capacity + pricing proposal, benchmark plan, and security docs by Aug 24. Auriga to provide logs, prompts, quota info by Aug 24. Benchmark run targeted week of Aug 31. Action owners noted.
[10:25] Ravi: Sounds good.
[10:28] Liam: Thanks everyone.
[10:30] Diego: Thanks.
[10:32] Sophie: Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions: e.g., 'KV cash' -> 'KV cache', 'Redwood Dedicate' -> 'Redwood Dedicated'. Timestamps are approximate and inserted every ~20-90 seconds to match call flow.
